purpose: Follow-up to the inconclusive actual-window latency comparison: isolate capture and one full validation, including per-thread CPU time and allocated bytes. This is not a whole-file-open measurement.

probe.compilation: javac --release 17 with the existing test/classes and dependency classpath, into a separate output directory; the same probe class is used by both production versions.

protocol.fixtureSource: The unchanged actual-window probe fixtures from the first baseline run, checked by SHA-256 on every load.
protocol.historyConstruction: The existing file-import prepareFileGame builder constructs the detached history. The diagnostic reads its private history field and attaches it to RulesLayerTestHarness on the EDT; no production API or installed application is modified.
protocol.execution: All iterations for one fixture run in one EDT task. Each iteration captures the current game, then calls isCurrent exactly once and requires true. Counter reads bracket each phase; row/JSON creation is outside the phase measurements.
protocol.accounting: ThreadMXBean current-thread CPU time and allocated bytes, plus elapsed time. Allocation is total bytes allocated by the EDT during the phase, not retained heap or peak process memory.
protocol.scope: Headless, no painting, engine updates, input interleaving or asynchronous file opening. Repeated warm reads of one history can have different cache/JIT behavior from interactive use.
protocol.otherWork: This task ran no builds or tests during these four timing JVMs. Shared-host load is uncontrolled. All retained observations, including slow/GC-affected samples, are included.
protocol.aggregation: Pool all 60 rows with sampleIndex >= 0 across both JVMs of a version, per fixture and metric; compute the median. Warmups remain in the raw rows.

candidatePublication.details: Published through the GitHub Git-object API. The published commit has exactly the same complete Git tree as the measured local commit; source blobs and all measurement artifact identities are unchanged.
